daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo announced readiness to cut the defence budget if necessary for the people, prompting a legislator to remind that the state budget should serve citizens. Separately, Prabowo also asked the public not to question TNI-Polri personnel working in rice fields. The president earlier pledged to provide higher education and job support for Sekolah Rakyat alumni during a visit to East Java.

  • Vice President Gibran inspected a Riau school to support the education revitalization drive, and separately responded to a teacher's Instagram comment about dilapidated schools by visiting MIN 1 Rokan Hilir to assess rehabilitation work and infrastructure needs.
  • Minister of State Apparatus Empowerment Rini wrote a letter to all civil servants urging them to continue serving even when their work goes unseen, asking them to keep serving despite personal fatigue and missing their families.
  • The DPR proposed state assistance for private universities in the National Education System Bill, while a DPR member separately urged refocusing the MBG programme to prioritize toddlers through junior high students and evaluate senior high school recipients.
  • A coalition of civil society organizations formed a shadow cabinet to monitor the government, with Tempo publishing the full list of shadow ministers.
  • The KPK identified high political costs as a trigger for corruption among regional heads, and proposed that the state fund campaign materials for election participants while suggesting campaigns shift to digital media to reduce costs.
  • Garda Prabowo withdrew its complaint against Tiyo Ardianto, saying the president has forgiven him, while characterizing Tiyo as smart but having chosen the wrong associates.
  • Deputy Chairman of the West Java DPRD rejected the proposal to introduce tuition fees at state senior high schools.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia strengthened border cooperation with Papua New Guinea through ministerial-level talks focused on cross-border electricity supply. The discussions aimed to enhance bilateral ties and address shared infrastructure challenges in the remote border region. Indonesia also promoted six hub airports to boost ASEAN-China air connectivity.

  • Coordinating Minister Airlangga stated that Indonesia sees room for both Chinese and US artificial intelligence initiatives, and separately said Indonesia can catch up in AI and robotics advancements.
  • Indonesia invited Huawei and ByteDance to boost artificial intelligence cooperation, while also backing the WAICO initiative to advance inclusive global AI governance, and Tempo reported Indonesia formally joined a global AI organization.
  • The Ministry of Tourism stepped up collaboration with the US Embassy in the gaming industry.
  • A DPR member asked the TNI to evaluate the location planning of ammunition warehouses, while a former general warned that TNI operations would be disrupted if the defence budget is reduced.

Other

The government announced Rp300 trillion in financing for micro enterprises, a major initiative to support small businesses across the country. This substantial allocation reflects the administration's focus on grassroots economic development. Meanwhile, the Ministry of Transportation received an unqualified audit opinion from BPK, with Minister Iftitah emphasizing public funds must be managed properly and beneficially.

  • Indonesia invited Chinese investors to participate in solar power plant projects, and separately is eyeing China and the Middle East for poultry exports.
  • The Minister of Education unveiled a seven-step strategy for violence-free schools, while separately the government announced steps to prevent violence in Islamic boarding schools.
  • A former PPATK head assessed that money laundering indicators are strong in the Febrie Adriansyah case, with Hotman Paris stating Febrie was criminalized without notice, while Kompas reported on FBI and Secret Service involvement in the case.
  • BRIN is preparing 177 policy research projects for 2026, while the Agriculture Minister said food security requires legal certainty over land rights.
  • The KPK will not appeal the verdict against John Field in the Customs bribery case, but left open the possibility of expanding the investigation.
